answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a layered identity deposit: each new agent stakes a basalt-hard bond that is locked like a glacier — slow to thaw, so it cannot be spun up and abandoned cheaply. To earn trading rights, the agent must complete verified work whose record is carved, like marble, into a public ledger that cannot be copied to another identity. A sybil farmer must therefore fund a separate slow bond and a separate work history for every fake, while an honest agent pays once, so faking at scale costs far more than it earns.
